standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md forbids scope notation; anti-patterns requires plain '<type>: <description>'. 4 commits use '(EPMCDME-14505)' scope suffix; 1 uses a branch slug as the type token.
.ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md is absent from the repo; no standard to adjudicate against
.ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md absent; concrete defects: (1) verify_download always None at downloader.rs:78; (2) dest path not validated before write at downloader.rs:79.

findings.title: Bundled shim invokes node.exe without existence check
findings.problem: codemie.cmd invokes %BUNDLE_DIR%\node\node.exe and the CLI entry-point unconditionally with no prior existence check on either file.
findings.impact: If either bundled file is absent the user receives a cryptic Windows 'The system cannot find the path specified' error with no installer-level diagnosis or recovery guidance.
findings.recommendation: Add `if not exist "%BUNDLE_DIR%\node\node.exe" (echo ERROR: bundled node.exe not found & exit /b 1)` before the invocation, and a parallel guard for the CLI entry-point.

findings.title: config_path ignores USERPROFILE on Windows
findings.problem: config_path() at line 96 resolves home via `std::env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default()` only; on Windows without Git for Windows or WSL, HOME is not set and the path becomes "/.codemie/codemie-cli.config.json".
findings.impact: read_codemie_config() silently returns CodemieConfig::default() (state=no-configuration) on stock Windows machines; the identity bar always shows 'CodeMie Desktop' regardless of whether a valid config file exists.
findings.recommendation: Use `std::env::var("HOME").or_else(|_| std::env::var("USERPROFILE")).unwrap_or_default()` so Windows machines without HOME fall back to USERPROFILE.

findings.title: Full download buffered in heap; Content-Length pre-alloc unsafeguarded
findings.problem: download_file accumulates all response bytes into Vec<u8> before writing to disk. Line 56 pre-allocates Vec::with_capacity(total as usize) from the untrusted Content-Length header; for 165-170 MB binaries this holds the entire file in heap before any bytes reach the filesystem. An adversarial Content-Length can exhaust address space before a single byte arrives.
findings.impact: OOM on memory-constrained machines for legitimate large downloads; a server returning a maliciously large Content-Length header crashes the installer process before the download completes.
findings.recommendation: Restore chunk-by-chunk streaming writes (AsyncWriteExt::write_all per chunk) to bound peak memory to one chunk; cap Vec pre-alloc: `resp.content_length().unwrap_or(0).min(512 * 1024 * 1024) as usize`.

findings.title: verify_download always called with expected_hash=None; SHA-256 never checked
findings.problem: The only production call to verify_download is `verify_download(&bytes, None)?` at line 78. The expected_hash parameter is hardcoded None; the SHA-256 verification code path is implemented but never reached. Every downloaded binary is accepted regardless of its content.
findings.impact: Downloaded executables are installed on end-user machines without integrity verification. A MITM attack or CDN substitution can deliver a malicious binary that passes all checks silently.
findings.recommendation: Add `expected_sha256: Option<String>` to the download_file IPC command signature and forward it into verify_download; callers that know the expected hash supply it; callers that do not pass None explicitly, accepting the risk.

findings.title: download_file writes to caller-supplied dest without path validation
findings.problem: `tokio::fs::write(&dest, &bytes)` at line 79 uses the dest String parameter verbatim; dest arrives directly from the IPC call with no canonicalization or prefix check.
findings.impact: A compromised renderer or injected IPC message can write arbitrary byte content to any path writable by the process, including per-user startup items or system configuration files.
findings.recommendation: Resolve dest against a safe root (e.g. app_data_dir() or a dedicated temp directory) and verify the canonical path remains within that root before writing; return InstallerError for any path that escapes the allowed prefix.

findings.title: global_version inline reimplementation deviates from spec; v-prefix version undetected
findings.problem: Spec requires populating global_version via check_codemie_version logic (inspector.rs:93-96); the implementation is an independent inline parser at handshake.rs:42-64. The custom parser requires all semver parts to be pure ASCII digits, so a 'v'-prefixed output ('v1.2.3') returns None even when global_found is true. The codemie --version subprocess is not injectable and no test asserts global_version in the found path.
findings.impact: UI receives global_found=true paired with global_version=None when the binary outputs a v-prefixed version string (common npm CLI format); HandshakeState is internally inconsistent and any precedence UI that branches on global_version will show the wrong state.
findings.recommendation: Replace the inline parser with a call to the existing parse_codemie_version/check_codemie_version logic from inspector.rs, or inject the version-query closure as a second parameter alongside probe so tests can assert global_version independently.

findings.title: Blocking std::process::Command in async IPC command
findings.problem: detect_handshake_state calls std::process::Command::new("codemie").arg("--version").output() at line 43, a blocking synchronous call. check_handshake_state (async fn, line 75) invokes it directly without wrapping in tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
findings.impact: If the codemie binary is present but slow to respond (first-launch JIT, NFS path, or anti-virus scan), the tokio worker thread is blocked for the full duration; concurrent IPC commands issued by the frontend are delayed or starved.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the detect_handshake_state call in spawn_blocking: `let state = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || detect_handshake_state(&path, injected, &real_probe)).await.map_err(|e| ...)?;`

findings.title: fetch_codemie_latest lacks required test coverage
findings.problem: The spec requires retaining or adding coverage for fetch_codemie_latest (installer.rs:89). The #[cfg(test)] module contains only parse_npm_latest tests; neither fetch_codemie_latest nor its helper fetch_codemie_npm_latest has any test.
findings.impact: The npm registry fetch path has no automated regression coverage; a change to the response shape, the Accept header, or the function logic will be silently undetected until runtime.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit test for fetch_codemie_npm_latest using a mock HTTP server or a test double for reqwest::Client, covering at least: successful parse, missing dist-tags key, and network error fallback to empty string.

findings.title: spawn_pty overwrites active PTY slot without killing prior child
findings.problem: spawn_pty unconditionally sets state.pty = Some((run_id, PtyHandle{...})) at lines 109-120 without first checking whether a PTY is already active. The prior PtyHandle is dropped in place without sending a kill signal.
findings.impact: The prior PTY child process is leaked and continues running; its reader thread emits stale engine:pty-data events with the old run_id, and its wait thread later emits a stale engine:pty-exit with the old run_id, which can corrupt the engine's step state.
findings.recommendation: Guard at entry: `if state.pty.lock().unwrap().is_some() { return Err(InstallerError::Pty("PTY already active".into())); }` or explicitly kill and await the prior child before replacing the slot.

findings.title: pty_kill targets current slot without validating run_id
findings.problem: pty_kill at line 197 matches the slot as `Some((_, h))`, discarding the stored run_id. If spawn_pty replaced the slot with a new process between the pty_kill IPC call and its execution, the new unrelated process is killed.
findings.impact: A race between a step completing (triggering pty_kill) and the next step spawning (triggering spawn_pty) kills the new process mid-run, leaving the engine in an inconsistent state with no recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Add a `run_id: String` parameter to pty_kill and use the clear_if_owner pattern already present in the file to validate the slot owner before acquiring the killer; return Ok(()) when the slot belongs to a different run.

findings.title: self_update_direct has no timeout; hangs indefinitely if node.exe stalls
findings.problem: self_update_direct calls `tokio::process::Command::new(node_exe).args([...]).output().await` at line 149 with no timeout wrapper; if node.exe hangs on startup the future never resolves.
findings.impact: The run_self_update IPC call never returns; the UI 'Updating...' spinner hangs indefinitely with no user escape path and no error surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Wrap with tokio::time::timeout: `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(120), Command::new(node_exe).args([...]).output()).await.map_err(|_| InstallerError::Other("self-update timed out".into()))?`.

findings.title: Windows batch file bundled into macOS DMG unconditionally
findings.problem: The bundle.resources entry at line 30 maps ../assets/windows/bin/codemie.cmd into all build targets including dmg (macOS) with no platform guard.
findings.impact: macOS DMG packages contain a Windows batch file that serves no purpose on macOS; may trigger Gatekeeper scrutiny or confuse users who inspect the app bundle contents.
findings.recommendation: Restrict the codemie.cmd resource to the nsis target using per-platform bundle configuration, or restructure tauri.conf.json to separate Windows-only resources from shared ones.

findings.title: Install Only wizard produces zero steps and silently completes as success
findings.problem: INSTALL_ONLY_IDS = ['1.1', '1.1.1', '1.3'] but all three step IDs were deleted from config/steps.yaml and config/steps-windows.yaml; the engine only knows ['2.3.3', '2.3.5', '2.4']. enterWizard(INSTALL_ONLY_IDS) at renderer.js:192 filters allSteps by INSTALL_ONLY_IDS and gets an empty array; engine.run() on an empty step set completes immediately and reports success.
findings.impact: Clicking the 'Install only' home tile opens the wizard with zero steps, shows a success screen without installing anything, and returns the user to the home view. The tile label still reads 'Install Git, Node & the CodeMie CLI'.
findings.recommendation: Either disable the 'Install only' tile (remove the data-action='install-only' element from index.html) or update INSTALL_ONLY_IDS to reference valid current step IDs that deliver the intended acquisition flow.

findings.title: Smoke probe safe-set references deleted step IDs; probe always passes
findings.problem: runProbe at line 607 filters engine.steps by `new Set(['1.1', '1.1.1', '1.2', '1.2.1', '1.3'])`; all five IDs were deleted from steps.yaml so the filter returns an empty array. engine.run() on an empty set emits PROBE_RESULT with an empty string and PROBE_DONE, always succeeding.
findings.impact: CODEMIE_PROBE_SMOKE=1 never performs any detection work; it unconditionally emits a false green. Testers relying on the probe to confirm codemie is present or absent receive no signal.
findings.recommendation: Update the safe-set to include current valid step IDs that cover the codemie detection path, or redesign the probe to call check_handshake_state directly instead of filtering the step engine.

findings.title: Five commits violate the documented commit-format standard
findings.problem: git-workflow.md explicitly forbids scope notation and requires plain '<type>: <description>'. Four commits use '(EPMCDME-14505)' as a parenthesised scope suffix on the type token. One commit ('EPMCDME-14573-windows-node-shim-runner-path: add planning artifacts') uses a branch slug as the type, matching none of the allowed conventional types (feat|fix|docs|test|chore|refactor).
findings.impact: Non-conforming commit history violates the project's documented anti-pattern list; automated or manual changelog tools relying on conventional-commit parsing will fail or misclassify these entries.
findings.recommendation: Reword the four scoped subjects by dropping the parenthesised scope (e.g., 'feat: add check_handshake_state IPC command') and reword the branch-slug subject to 'chore: EPMCDME-14573 planning artifacts'.
